sanskrit_shloka:
उपाधिरायाति स एव गच्छति स एव कर्माणि करोति भुङ्क्ते ।
स एव जीर्यन्म्रियते सदाहं कुलाद्रिवन्निश्चल एव संस्थितः ॥ ५0१ ॥
transliteration:
upādhirāyāti sa eva gacchati sa eva karmāṇi karoti bhuṅkte |
sa eva jīryanmriyate sadāhaṃ kulādrivanniścala eva saṃsthitaḥ || 501 ||
translation: It is the Upādhi (superimposed attribute) that comes, and it is that alone which goes; that, again, performs actions and experiences (their fruits), that alone decays and dies, whereas I ever remain firm like the Kula mountain.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: It is the Upādhi (superimposed attribute) that comes, and it is that alone which goes; that, again, performs actions and experiences (their fruits), that alone decays and dies, whereas I ever remain firm like the Kula mountain.

sanskrit_shloka:
न मे प्रवृत्तिर्न च मे निवृत्तिः सदैकरूपस्य निरंशकस्य ।
एकात्मको यो निविडो निरन्तरो व्योमेव पूर्णः स कथं नु चेष्टते ॥ ५0२ ॥
transliteration:
na me pravṛttirna ca me nivṛttiḥ sadaikarūpasya niraṃśakasya |
ekātmako yo niviḍo nirantaro vyomeva pūrṇaḥ sa kathaṃ nu ceṣṭate || 502 ||
translation: There is neither engaging in work nor cessation from it, for me who am always the same and devoid of parts, there is neither engaging in work nor cessation from it. How can that which is One, concentrated, without break and infinite like the sky, ever exert?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: There is neither engaging in work nor cessation from it, for me who am always the same and devoid of parts, there is neither engaging in work nor cessation from it. How can that which is One, concentrated, without break and infinite like the sky, ever exert?

sanskrit_shloka:
पुण्यानि पापानि निरिन्द्रियस्य निश्चेतसो निर्विकृतेर्निराकृतेः ।
कुतो ममाखण्डसुखानुभूतेः ब्रूते ह्यनन्वागतमित्यपि श्रुतिः ॥ ५0३ ॥
transliteration:
puṇyāni pāpāni nirindriyasya niścetaso nirvikṛternirākṛteḥ |
kuto mamākhaṇḍasukhānubhūteḥ brūte hyananvāgatamityapi śrutiḥ || 503 ||
translation: How can there be merits and demerits for me, who am without organs, without mind, changeless, and formless – who am the realisation of Bliss Absolute? The Shruti also mentions this in the passage 'Not touched', etc.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: How can there be merits and demerits for me, who am without organs, without mind, changeless, and formless – who am the realisation of Bliss Absolute? The Shruti also mentions this in the passage 'Not touched', etc.

sanskrit_shloka:
छायया स्पृष्टमुष्णं वा शीतं वा सुष्ठु दुःष्ठु वा ।
न स्पृशत्येव यत्किंचित्पुरुषं तद्विलक्षणम् ॥ ५0४ ॥
transliteration:
chāyayā spṛṣṭamuṣṇaṃ vā śītaṃ vā suṣṭhu duḥṣṭhu vā |
na spṛśatyeva yatkiṃcitpuruṣaṃ tadvilakṣaṇam || 504 ||
translation: If heat or cold, or good or evil, happens to touch the shadow of a man’s body, it affects not in the least the man himself, who is distinct from the shadow.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: If heat or cold, or good or evil, happens to touch the shadow of a man’s body, it affects not in the least the man himself, who is distinct from the shadow.

sanskrit_shloka:
न साक्षिणं साक्ष्यधर्माः संस्पृशन्ति विलक्षणम् ।
अविकारमुदासीनं गृहधर्माः प्रदीपवत् ॥ ५0५ ॥
transliteration:
na sākṣiṇaṃ sākṣyadharmāḥ saṃspṛśanti vilakṣaṇam |
avikāramudāsīnaṃ gṛhadharmāḥ pradīpavat || 505 ||
translation: The properties of things observed do not affect the Witness, which is distinct from them, changeless and indifferent – as the properties of a room (do not affect) the lamp (that illumines it).

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The properties of things observed do not affect the Witness, which is distinct from them, changeless and indifferent – as the properties of a room (do not affect) the lamp (that illumines it).

sanskrit_shloka:
रवेर्यथा कर्मणि साक्षिभावो वन्हेर्यथा दाहनियामकत्वम् ।
रज्जोर्यथारोपितवस्तुसङ्गः तथैव कूटस्थचिदात्मनो मे ॥ ५0६ ॥
transliteration:
raveryathā karmaṇi sākṣibhāvo vanheryathā dāhaniyāmakatvam |
rajjoryathāropitavastusaṅgaḥ tathaiva kūṭasthacidātmano me || 506 ||
translation: As the sun is a mere witness of men’s actions, as fire burns everything without distinction, and as the rope is related to a thing superimposed on it, so am I, the unchangeable Self, the Intelligence Absolute.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: As the sun is a mere witness of men’s actions, as fire burns everything without distinction, and as the rope is related to a thing superimposed on it, so am I, the unchangeable Self, the Intelligence Absolute.

sanskrit_shloka:
कर्तापि वा कारयितापि नाहं भोक्तापि वा भोजयितापि नाहम् ।
द्रष्टापि वा दर्शयितापि नाहं सोऽहं स्वयंज्योतिरनीदृगात्मा ॥ ५0७ ॥
transliteration:
kartāpi vā kārayitāpi nāhaṃ bhoktāpi vā bhojayitāpi nāham |
draṣṭāpi vā darśayitāpi nāhaṃ so'haṃ svayaṃjyotiranīdṛgātmā || 507 ||
translation: I neither do nor make others do any action; I neither enjoy nor make others enjoy; I neither see nor make others see; I am that Self-effulgent, Transcendent Ātman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I neither do nor make others do any action; I neither enjoy nor make others enjoy; I neither see nor make others see; I am that Self-effulgent, Transcendent Ātman.

sanskrit_shloka:
चलत्युपाधौ प्रतिबिम्बलौल्यम् अउपाधिकं मूढधियो नयन्ति ।
स्वबिम्बभूतं रविवद्विनिष्क्रियं कर्तास्मि भोक्तास्मि हतोऽस्मि हेति ॥ ५0८ ॥
transliteration:
calatyupādhau pratibimbalaulyam aupādhikaṃ mūḍhadhiyo nayanti |
svabimbabhūtaṃ ravivadviniṣkriyaṃ kartāsmi bhoktāsmi hato'smi heti || 508 ||
translation: When the supervening adjunct (Upādhi) is moving, the resulting movement of the reflection is ascribed by fools to the object reflected, such as the sun, which is free from activity – (and they think) 'I am the doer', 'I am the experiencer', 'I am killed, oh, alas!'

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the supervening adjunct (Upādhi) is moving, the resulting movement of the reflection is ascribed by fools to the object reflected, such as the sun, which is free from activity – (and they think) 'I am the doer', 'I am the experiencer', 'I am killed, oh, alas!'

sanskrit_shloka:
जले वापि स्थले वापि लुठत्वेष जडात्मकः ।
नाहं विलिप्ये तद्धर्मैर्घटधर्मैर्नभो यथा ॥ ५0९ ॥
transliteration:
jale vāpi sthale vāpi luṭhatveṣa jaḍātmakaḥ |
nāhaṃ vilipye taddharmairghaṭadharmairnabho yathā || 509 ||
translation: Let this inert body drop down in water or on land. I am not touched by its properties, like the sky by the properties of the jar.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Let this inert body drop down in water or on land. I am not touched by its properties, like the sky by the properties of the jar.

sanskrit_shloka:
कर्तृत्वभोक्तृत्वखलत्वमत्तता जडत्वबद्धत्वविमुक्ततादयः ।
बुद्धेर्विकल्पा न तु सन्ति वस्तुतः स्वस्मिन् परे ब्रह्मणि केवलेऽद्वये ॥ ५१0 ॥
transliteration:
kartṛtvabhoktṛtvakhalatvamattatā jaḍatvabaddhatvavimuktatādayaḥ |
buddhervikalpā na tu santi vastutaḥ svasmin pare brahmaṇi kevale'dvaye || 510 ||
translation: The passing states of the Buddhi, such as agency, experience, cunning, drunkenness, dullness, bondage and freedom, are never in reality in the Self, the Supreme Brahman, the Absolute, the one without a second.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The passing states of the Buddhi, such as agency, experience, cunning, drunkenness, dullness, bondage and freedom, are never in reality in the Self, the Supreme Brahman, the Absolute, the one without a second.

sanskrit_shloka:
सन्तु विकाराः प्रकृतेर्दशधा शतधा सहस्रधा वापि ।
किं मेऽसङ्गचितस्तैर्न घनः क्वचिदम्बरं स्पृशति ॥ ५११ ॥
transliteration:
santu vikārāḥ prakṛterdaśadhā śatadhā sahasradhā vāpi |
kiṃ me'saṅgacitastairna ghanaḥ kvacidambaraṃ spṛśati || 511 ||
translation: Let there be changes in the Prakriti in ten, a hundred, or a thousand ways, what have I, the unattached Knowledge Absolute, got to do with them? Never do the clouds touch the sky!

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Let there be changes in the Prakriti in ten, a hundred, or a thousand ways, what have I, the unattached Knowledge Absolute, got to do with them? Never do the clouds touch the sky!

sanskrit_shloka:
अव्यक्तादिस्थूलपर्यन्तमेतत् विश्व यत्राभासमात्रं प्रतीतम् ।
व्योमप्रख्यं सूक्ष्ममाद्यन्तहीनं ब्रह्माद्वैतं यत्तदेवाहमस्मि ॥ ५१२ ॥
transliteration:
avyaktādisthūlaparyantametat viśva yatrābhāsamātraṃ pratītam |
vyomaprakhyaṃ sūkṣmamādyantahīnaṃ brahmādvaitaṃ yattadevāhamasmi || 512 ||
translation: I am verily that Brahman, the One without a second, which is like the sky, subtle, without beginning or end, in which the whole universe from the Undifferentiated down to the gross body, appears merely as a shadow.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am verily that Brahman, the One without a second, which is like the sky, subtle, without beginning or end, in which the whole universe from the Undifferentiated down to the gross body, appears merely as a shadow.

sanskrit_shloka:
सर्वाधारं सर्ववस्तुप्रकाशं सर्वाकारं सर्वगं सर्वशून्यम् ।
नित्यं शुद्धं निश्चलं निर्विकल्पं ब्रह्माद्वैतं यत्तदेवाहमस्मि ॥ ५१३ ॥
transliteration:
sarvādhāraṃ sarvavastuprakāśaṃ sarvākāraṃ sarvagaṃ sarvaśūnyam |
nityaṃ śuddhaṃ niścalaṃ nirvikalpaṃ brahmādvaitaṃ yattadevāhamasmi || 513 ||
translation: I am verily that Brahman, the One without a second, which is the support of all, which illumines all things, which has infinite forms, is omnipresent, devoid of multiplicity, eternal, pure, unmoved and absolute.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am verily that Brahman, the One without a second, which is the support of all, which illumines all things, which has infinite forms, is omnipresent, devoid of multiplicity, eternal, pure, unmoved and absolute.

sanskrit_shloka:
यत्प्रत्यस्ताशेषमायाविशेषं प्रत्यग्रूपं प्रत्ययागम्यमानम् ।
सत्यज्ञानानन्तमानन्दरूपं ब्रह्माद्वैतं यत्तदेवाहमस्मि ॥ ५१४ ॥
transliteration:
yatpratyastāśeṣamāyāviśeṣaṃ pratyagrūpaṃ pratyayāgamyamānam |
satyajñānānantamānandarūpaṃ brahmādvaitaṃ yattadevāhamasmi || 514 ||
translation: I am verily that Brahman, the One without a second, which transcends the endless differentiations of Māyā, which is the inmost essence of all, is beyond the range of consciousness, and which is Truth, Knowledge, Infinity and Bliss Absolute.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am verily that Brahman, the One without a second, which transcends the endless differentiations of Māyā, which is the inmost essence of all, is beyond the range of consciousness, and which is Truth, Knowledge, Infinity and Bliss Absolute.

sanskrit_shloka:
निष्क्रियोऽस्म्यविकारोऽस्मि निष्कलोऽस्मि निराकृतिः ।
निर्विकल्पोऽस्मि नित्योऽस्मि निरालम्बोऽस्मि निर्द्वयः ॥ ५१५ ॥
transliteration:
niṣkriyo'smyavikāro'smi niṣkalo'smi nirākṛtiḥ |
nirvikalpo'smi nityo'smi nirālambo'smi nirdvayaḥ || 515 ||
translation: I am without activity, changeless, without parts, formless, absolute, eternal, without any other support, the One without a second.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am without activity, changeless, without parts, formless, absolute, eternal, without any other support, the One without a second.

sanskrit_shloka:
सर्वात्मकोऽहं सर्वोऽहं सर्वातीतोऽहमद्वयः ।
केवलाक्षण्डबोधोऽहमानन्दोऽहं निरन्तरः ॥ ५१६ ॥
transliteration:
sarvātmako'haṃ sarvo'haṃ sarvātīto'hamadvayaḥ |
kevalākṣaṇḍabodho'hamānando'haṃ nirantaraḥ || 516 ||
translation: I am the Universal, I am the All, I am transcendent, the One without a second. I am Absolute and Infinite Knowledge, I am Bliss and indivisible.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am the Universal, I am the All, I am transcendent, the One without a second. I am Absolute and Infinite Knowledge, I am Bliss and indivisible.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वाराज्यसाम्राज्यविभूतिरेषा भवत्कृपाश्रीमहिमप्रसादात् ।
प्राप्ता मया श्रीगुरवे महात्मने नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु पुनर्नमोऽस्तु ॥ ५१७ ॥
transliteration:
svārājyasāmrājyavibhūtireṣā bhavatkṛpāśrīmahimaprasādāt |
prāptā mayā śrīgurave mahātmane namo namaste'stu punarnamo'stu || 517 ||
translation: This splendour of the sovereignty of Self-effulgence I have received by virtue of the supreme majesty of thy grace. Salutations to thee, O glorious, noble-minded Teacher, salutations again and again!

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This splendour of the sovereignty of Self-effulgence I have received by virtue of the supreme majesty of thy grace. Salutations to thee, O glorious, noble-minded Teacher, salutations again and again!

sanskrit_shloka:
महास्वप्ने मायाकृतजनिजरामृत्युगहने भ्रमन्तं क्लिश्यन्तं बहुलतरतापैरनुदिनम् ।
अहंकारव्याघ्रव्यथितमिममत्यन्तकृपया प्रबोध्य प्रस्वापात्परमवितवान्मामसि गुरो ॥ ५१८ ॥
transliteration:
mahāsvapne māyākṛtajanijarāmṛtyugahane bhramantaṃ kliśyantaṃ bahulataratāpairanudinam |
ahaṃkāravyāghravyathitamimamatyantakṛpayā prabodhya prasvāpātparamavitavānmāmasi guro || 518 ||
translation: O Master, thou hast out of sheer grace awakened me from sleep and completely saved me, who was wandering, in an interminable dream, in a forest of birth, decay and death created by illusion, being tormented day after day by countless afflictions, and sorely troubled by the tiger of egoism.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: O Master, thou hast out of sheer grace awakened me from sleep and completely saved me, who was wandering, in an interminable dream, in a forest of birth, decay and death created by illusion, being tormented day after day by countless afflictions, and sorely troubled by the tiger of egoism.

sanskrit_shloka:
नमस्तस्मै सदैकस्मै कस्मैचिन्महसे नमः ।
यदेतद्विश्वरूपेण राजते गुरुराज ते ॥ ५१९ ॥
transliteration:
namastasmai sadaikasmai kasmaicinmahase namaḥ |
yadetadviśvarūpeṇa rājate gururāja te || 519 ||
translation: Salutations to thee, O Prince of Teachers, thou unnamable Greatness, that art ever the same and dost manifest thyself as this universe – thee I salute.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Salutations to thee, O Prince of Teachers, thou unnamable Greatness, that art ever the same and dost manifest thyself as this universe – thee I salute.

sanskrit_shloka:
इति नतमवलोक्य शिष्यवर्यं समधिगतात्मसुखं प्रबुद्धतत्त्वम् ।
प्रमुदितहृदयं स देशिकेन्द्रः पुनरिदमाह वचः परं महात्मा ॥ ५२0 ॥
transliteration:
iti natamavalokya śiṣyavaryaṃ samadhigatātmasukhaṃ prabuddhatattvam |
pramuditahṛdayaṃ sa deśikendraḥ punaridamāha vacaḥ paraṃ mahātmā || 520 ||
translation: Seeing the worthy disciple, who had attained the Bliss of the self, realised the Truth and was glad at heart, thus prostrating himself, that noble, ideal Teacher again addressed the following excellent words:

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Seeing the worthy disciple, who had attained the Bliss of the self, realised the Truth and was glad at heart, thus prostrating himself, that noble, ideal Teacher again addressed the following excellent words:

sanskrit_shloka:
ब्रह्मप्रत्ययसन्ततिर्जगदतो ब्रह्मैव तत्सर्वतः पश्याध्यात्मदृशा प्रशान्तमनसा सर्वास्ववस्थास्वपि ।
रूपादन्यदवेक्षितं किमभितश्चक्षुष्मतां दृश्यते तद्वद्ब्रह्मविदः सतः किमपरं बुद्धेर्विहारास्पदम् ॥ ५२१ ॥
transliteration:
brahmapratyayasantatirjagadato brahmaiva tatsarvataḥ paśyādhyātmadṛśā praśāntamanasā sarvāsvavasthāsvapi |
rūpādanyadavekṣitaṃ kimabhitaścakṣuṣmatāṃ dṛśyate tadvadbrahmavidaḥ sataḥ kimaparaṃ buddhervihārāspadam || 521 ||
translation: The universe is an unbroken series of perceptions of Brahman; hence it is in all respects nothing but Brahman. See this with the eye of illumination and a serene mind, under all circumstances. Is one who has eyes ever found to see all around anything else but forms? Similarly, what is there except Brahman to engage the intellect of a man of realisation?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The universe is an unbroken series of perceptions of Brahman; hence it is in all respects nothing but Brahman. See this with the eye of illumination and a serene mind, under all circumstances. Is one who has eyes ever found to see all around anything else but forms? Similarly, what is there except Brahman to engage the intellect of a man of realisation?

sanskrit_shloka:
कस्तां परानन्दरसानुभूति मृत्सृज्य शून्येषु रमेत विद्वान् ।
चन्द्रे महाल्हादिनि दीप्यमाने चित्रेन्दुमालोकयितुं क इच्छेत् ॥ ५२२ ॥
transliteration:
kastāṃ parānandarasānubhūti mṛtsṛjya śūnyeṣu rameta vidvān |
candre mahālhādini dīpyamāne citrendumālokayituṃ ka icchet || 522 ||
translation: What wise man would discard that enjoyment of Supreme Bliss and revel in things unsubstantial? When the exceedingly charming moon is shining, who would wish to look at a painted moon?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: What wise man would discard that enjoyment of Supreme Bliss and revel in things unsubstantial? When the exceedingly charming moon is shining, who would wish to look at a painted moon?

sanskrit_shloka:
असत्पदार्थानुभवेन किंचिन् न ह्यस्ति तृप्तिर्न च दुःखहानिः ।
तदद्वयानन्दरसानुभूत्या तृप्तः सुखं तिष्ठ सदात्मनिष्ठया ॥ ५२३ ॥
transliteration:
asatpadārthānubhavena kiṃcin na hyasti tṛptirna ca duḥkhahāniḥ |
tadadvayānandarasānubhūtyā tṛptaḥ sukhaṃ tiṣṭha sadātmaniṣṭhayā || 523 ||
translation: From the perception of unreal things there is neither satisfaction nor a cessation of misery. Therefore, being satisfied with the realisation of the Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, live happily in a state of identity with that Reality.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: From the perception of unreal things there is neither satisfaction nor a cessation of misery. Therefore, being satisfied with the realisation of the Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, live happily in a state of identity with that Reality.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वमेव सर्वथा पश्यन्मन्यमानः स्वमद्वयम् ।
स्वानन्दमनुभुञ्जानः कालं नय महामते ॥ ५२४ ॥
transliteration:
svameva sarvathā paśyanmanyamānaḥ svamadvayam |
svānandamanubhuñjānaḥ kālaṃ naya mahāmate || 524 ||
translation: Beholding the Self alone in all circumstances, thinking of the Self, the One without a second, and enjoying the Bliss of the Self, pass thy time, O noble soul!

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Beholding the Self alone in all circumstances, thinking of the Self, the One without a second, and enjoying the Bliss of the Self, pass thy time, O noble soul!

sanskrit_shloka:
अखण्डबोधात्मनि निर्विकल्पे विकल्पनं व्योम्नि पुरप्रकल्पनम् ।
तदद्वयानन्दमयात्मना सदा शान्तिं परामेत्य भजस्व मौनम् ॥ ५२५ ॥
transliteration:
akhaṇḍabodhātmani nirvikalpe vikalpanaṃ vyomni puraprakalpanam |
tadadvayānandamayātmanā sadā śāntiṃ parāmetya bhajasva maunam || 525 ||
translation: Dualistic conceptions in the Ātman, the Infinite Knowledge, the Absolute, are like imagining castles in the air. Therefore, always identifying thyself with the Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, and thereby attaining Supreme Peace, remain quiet.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Dualistic conceptions in the Ātman, the Infinite Knowledge, the Absolute, are like imagining castles in the air. Therefore, always identifying thyself with the Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, and thereby attaining Supreme Peace, remain quiet.

sanskrit_shloka:
तूष्णीमवस्था परमोपशान्तिः बुद्धेरसत्कल्पविकल्पहेतोः ।
ब्रह्मात्मन ब्रह्मविदो महात्मनो यत्राद्वयानन्दसुखं निरन्तरम् ॥ ५२६ ॥
transliteration:
tūṣṇīmavasthā paramopaśāntiḥ buddherasatkalpavikalpahetoḥ |
brahmātmana brahmavido mahātmano yatrādvayānandasukhaṃ nirantaram || 526 ||
translation: To the sage who has realised Brahman, the mind, which is the cause of unreal fancies, becomes perfectly tranquil. This verily is his state of quietude, in which, identified with Brahman, he has constant enjoyment of the Bliss Absolute, the One without a second.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: To the sage who has realised Brahman, the mind, which is the cause of unreal fancies, becomes perfectly tranquil. This verily is his state of quietude, in which, identified with Brahman, he has constant enjoyment of the Bliss Absolute, the One without a second.

sanskrit_shloka:
नास्ति निर्वासनान्मौनात्परं सुखकृदुत्तमम् ।
विज्ञातात्मस्वरूपस्य स्वानन्दरसपायिनः ॥ ५२७ ॥
transliteration:
nāsti nirvāsanānmaunātparaṃ sukhakṛduttamam |
vijñātātmasvarūpasya svānandarasapāyinaḥ || 527 ||
translation: To the man who has realised his own nature, and drinks the undiluted Bliss of the Self, there is nothing more exhilarating than the quietude that comes of a state of desirelessness.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: To the man who has realised his own nature, and drinks the undiluted Bliss of the Self, there is nothing more exhilarating than the quietude that comes of a state of desirelessness.

sanskrit_shloka:
गच्छंस्तिष्ठन्नुपविशञ्छयानो वान्यथापि वा ।
यथेच्छया वेसेद्विद्वानात्नारामः सदा मुनिः ॥ ५२८ ॥
transliteration:
gacchaṃstiṣṭhannupaviśañchayāno vānyathāpi vā |
yathecchayā vesedvidvānātnārāmaḥ sadā muniḥ || 528 ||
translation: The illumined sage, whose only pleasure is in the Self, ever lives at ease, whether going or staying, sitting or lying, or in any other condition.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The illumined sage, whose only pleasure is in the Self, ever lives at ease, whether going or staying, sitting or lying, or in any other condition.

sanskrit_shloka:
न देशकालासनदिग्यमादि लक्ष्याद्यपेक्षाप्रतिबद्धवृत्तेः ।
संसिद्धतत्त्वस्य महात्मनोऽस्ति स्ववेदने का नियमाद्यवस्था ॥ ५२९ ॥
transliteration:
na deśakālāsanadigyamādi lakṣyādyapekṣāpratibaddhavṛtteḥ |
saṃsiddhatattvasya mahātmano'sti svavedane kā niyamādyavasthā || 529 ||
translation: The noble soul who has perfectly realised the Truth, and whose mind-functions meet with no obstruction, no more depends upon conditions of place, time, posture, direction, moral disciplines, objects of meditation and so forth. What regulative conditions can there be in knowing one’s own Self?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The noble soul who has perfectly realised the Truth, and whose mind-functions meet with no obstruction, no more depends upon conditions of place, time, posture, direction, moral disciplines, objects of meditation and so forth. What regulative conditions can there be in knowing one’s own Self?

sanskrit_shloka:
घटोऽयमिति विज्ञातुं नियमः कोऽन्ववेक्षते ।
विना प्रमाणसुष्ठुत्वं यस्मिन् सति पदार्थधीः ॥ ५३0 ॥
transliteration:
ghaṭo'yamiti vijñātuṃ niyamaḥ ko'nvavekṣate |
vinā pramāṇasuṣṭhutvaṃ yasmin sati padārthadhīḥ || 530 ||
translation: To know that this is a jar, what condition, forsooth, is necessary except that the means of knowledge be free from defect, which alone ensures a cognition of the object?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: To know that this is a jar, what condition, forsooth, is necessary except that the means of knowledge be free from defect, which alone ensures a cognition of the object?

sanskrit_shloka:
अयमात्मा नित्यसिद्धः प्रमाणे सति भासते ।
न देशं नापि कालं न शुद्धिं वाप्यपेक्षते ॥ ५३१ ॥
transliteration:
ayamātmā nityasiddhaḥ pramāṇe sati bhāsate |
na deśaṃ nāpi kālaṃ na śuddhiṃ vāpyapekṣate || 531 ||
translation: So this Ātman, which is an eternal verity, manifests Itself as soon as the right means of knowledge is present, and does not depend upon either place or time or (internal) purity.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: So this Ātman, which is an eternal verity, manifests Itself as soon as the right means of knowledge is present, and does not depend upon either place or time or (internal) purity.

sanskrit_shloka:
देवदत्तोऽहमित्येतद्विज्ञानं निरपेक्षकम् ।
तद्वद्ब्रह्मविदोऽप्यस्य ब्रह्माहमिति वेदनम् ॥ ५३२ ॥
transliteration:
devadatto'hamityetadvijñānaṃ nirapekṣakam |
tadvadbrahmavido'pyasya brahmāhamiti vedanam || 532 ||
translation: The consciousness, 'I am Devadatta', is independent of circumstances; similar is the case with the realisation of the knower of Brahman that he is Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The consciousness, 'I am Devadatta', is independent of circumstances; similar is the case with the realisation of the knower of Brahman that he is Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
भानुनेव जगत्सर्वं भासते यस्य तेजसा ।
अनात्मकमसत्तुच्छं किं नु तस्यावभासकम् ॥ ५३३ ॥
transliteration:
bhānuneva jagatsarvaṃ bhāsate yasya tejasā |
anātmakamasattucchaṃ kiṃ nu tasyāvabhāsakam || 533 ||
translation: What indeed can manifest That whose lustre, like the sun, causes the whole universe – unsubstantial, unreal, insignificant – to appear at all?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: What indeed can manifest That whose lustre, like the sun, causes the whole universe – unsubstantial, unreal, insignificant – to appear at all?

sanskrit_shloka:
वेदशास्त्रपुराणानि भूतानि सकलान्यपि ।
येनार्थवन्ति तं किन्नु विज्ञातारं प्रकाशयेत् ॥ ५३४ ॥
transliteration:
vedaśāstrapurāṇāni bhūtāni sakalānyapi |
yenārthavanti taṃ kinnu vijñātāraṃ prakāśayet || 534 ||
translation: What, indeed, can illumine that Eternal Subject by which the Vedas and Puranas and other Scriptures, as well as all beings are endowed with a meaning?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: What, indeed, can illumine that Eternal Subject by which the Vedas and Puranas and other Scriptures, as well as all beings are endowed with a meaning?

sanskrit_shloka:
एष स्वयंज्योतिरनन्तशक्तिः आत्माप्रमेयः सकलानुभूतिः ।
यमेव विज्ञाय विमुक्तबन्धो जयत्ययं ब्रह्मविदुत्तमोत्तमः ॥ ५३५ ॥
transliteration:
eṣa svayaṃjyotiranantaśaktiḥ ātmāprameyaḥ sakalānubhūtiḥ |
yameva vijñāya vimuktabandho jayatyayaṃ brahmaviduttamottamaḥ || 535 ||
translation: Here is the Self-effulgent Ātman, of infinite power, beyond the range of conditioned knowledge, yet the common experience of all - realising which alone this incomparable knower of Brahman lives his glorious life, freed from bondage.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Here is the Self-effulgent Ātman, of infinite power, beyond the range of conditioned knowledge, yet the common experience of all - realising which alone this incomparable knower of Brahman lives his glorious life, freed from bondage.

sanskrit_shloka:
न खिद्यते नो विषयैः प्रमोदते न सज्जते नापि विरज्यते च ।
स्वस्मिन्सदा क्रीडति नन्दति स्वयं निरन्तरानन्दरसेन तृप्तः ॥ ५३६ ॥
transliteration:
na khidyate no viṣayaiḥ pramodate na sajjate nāpi virajyate ca |
svasminsadā krīḍati nandati svayaṃ nirantarānandarasena tṛptaḥ || 536 ||
translation: Satisfied with undiluted, constant Bliss, he is neither grieved nor elated by sense- objects, is neither attached nor averse to them, but always disports with the Self and takes pleasure therein.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Satisfied with undiluted, constant Bliss, he is neither grieved nor elated by sense- objects, is neither attached nor averse to them, but always disports with the Self and takes pleasure therein.

sanskrit_shloka:
क्षुधां देहव्यथां त्यक्त्वा बालः क्रीडति वस्तुनिः ।
तथैव विद्वान् रमते निर्ममो निरहं सुखी ॥ ५३७ ॥
transliteration:
kṣudhāṃ dehavyathāṃ tyaktvā bālaḥ krīḍati vastuniḥ |
tathaiva vidvān ramate nirmamo nirahaṃ sukhī || 537 ||
translation: A child plays with its toys forgetting hunger and bodily pains; exactly so does the man of realisation take pleasure in the Reality, without ideas of 'I' or 'mine', and is happy.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: A child plays with its toys forgetting hunger and bodily pains; exactly so does the man of realisation take pleasure in the Reality, without ideas of 'I' or 'mine', and is happy.

sanskrit_shloka:
चिन्ताशून्यमदैन्यभैक्षमशनं पानं सरिद्वारिषु स्वातन्त्र्येण निरङ्कुशा स्थितिरभीर्निद्रा श्मशाने वने ।
वस्त्रं क्षालनशोषणादिरहितं दिग्वास्तु शय्या मही संचारो निगमान्तवीथिषु विदां क्रीडा परे ब्रह्मणि ॥ ५३८ ॥
transliteration:
cintāśūnyamadainyabhaikṣamaśanaṃ pānaṃ saridvāriṣu svātantryeṇa niraṅkuśā sthitirabhīrnidrā śmaśāne vane |
vastraṃ kṣālanaśoṣaṇādirahitaṃ digvāstu śayyā mahī saṃcāro nigamāntavīthiṣu vidāṃ krīḍā pare brahmaṇi || 538 ||
translation: Men of realisation have their food without anxiety or humiliation by begging, and their drink from the water of rivers; they live freely and independently, and sleep without fear in cremation grounds or forests; their clothing may be the quarters themselves, which need no washing and drying, or any bark etc., the earth is their bed; they roam in the avenue of the Vedanta; while their pastime is in the Supreme Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Men of realisation have their food without anxiety or humiliation by begging, and their drink from the water of rivers; they live freely and independently, and sleep without fear in cremation grounds or forests; their clothing may be the quarters themselves, which need no washing and drying, or any bark etc., the earth is their bed; they roam in the avenue of the Vedanta; while their pastime is in the Supreme Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
विमानमालम्ब्य शरीरमेतद् भुनक्त्यशेषान्विषयानुपस्थितान् ।
परेच्छया बालवदात्मवेत्ता योऽव्यक्तलिङ्गोऽननुषक्तबाह्यः ॥ ५३९ ॥
transliteration:
vimānamālambya śarīrametad bhunaktyaśeṣānviṣayānupasthitān |
parecchayā bālavadātmavettā yo'vyaktaliṅgo'nanuṣaktabāhyaḥ || 539 ||
translation: The knower of the Ātman, who wears no outward mark and is unattached to external things, rests on this body without identification, and experiences all sorts of sense-objects as they come, through others’ wish, like a child.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The knower of the Ātman, who wears no outward mark and is unattached to external things, rests on this body without identification, and experiences all sorts of sense-objects as they come, through others’ wish, like a child.

sanskrit_shloka:
दिगम्बरो वापि च साम्बरो वा त्वगम्बरो वापि चिदम्बरस्थः ।
उन्मत्तवद्वापि च बालवद्वा पिशाचवद्वापि चरत्यवन्याम् ॥ ५४0 ॥
transliteration:
digambaro vāpi ca sāmbaro vā tvagambaro vāpi cidambarasthaḥ |
unmattavadvāpi ca bālavadvā piśācavadvāpi caratyavanyām || 540 ||
translation: Established in the ethereal plane of Absolute Knowledge, he wanders in the world, sometimes like a madman, sometimes like a child and at other times like a ghoul, having no other clothes on his person except the quarters, or sometimes wearing clothes, or perhaps skins at other times.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Established in the ethereal plane of Absolute Knowledge, he wanders in the world, sometimes like a madman, sometimes like a child and at other times like a ghoul, having no other clothes on his person except the quarters, or sometimes wearing clothes, or perhaps skins at other times.

sanskrit_shloka:
कामान्निष्कामरूपी संश्चरत्येकचारो मुनिः ।
स्वात्मनैव सदा तुष्टः स्वयं सर्वात्मना स्थितः ॥ ५४१ ॥
transliteration:
kāmānniṣkāmarūpī saṃścaratyekacāro muniḥ |
svātmanaiva sadā tuṣṭaḥ svayaṃ sarvātmanā sthitaḥ || 541 ||
translation: The sage, living alone, enjoys the sense-objects, being the very embodiment of desirelessness – always satisfied with his own Self, and himself present at the All.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The sage, living alone, enjoys the sense-objects, being the very embodiment of desirelessness – always satisfied with his own Self, and himself present at the All.

sanskrit_shloka:
क्वचिन्मूढो विद्वान् क्वचिदपि महाराजविभवः क्वचिद्भ्रान्तः सौम्यः क्वचिदजगराचारकलितः ।
क्वचित्पात्रीभूतः क्वचिदवमतः क्वाप्यविदितः चरत्येवं प्राज्ञः सततपरमानन्दसुखितः ॥ ५४२ ॥
transliteration:
kvacinmūḍho vidvān kvacidapi mahārājavibhavaḥ kvacidbhrāntaḥ saumyaḥ kvacidajagarācārakalitaḥ |
kvacitpātrībhūtaḥ kvacidavamataḥ kvāpyaviditaḥ caratyevaṃ prājñaḥ satataparamānandasukhitaḥ || 542 ||
translation: Sometimes a fool, sometimes a sage, sometimes possessed of regal splendour; sometimes wandering, sometimes behaving like a motionless python, sometimes wearing a benignant expression; sometimes honoured, sometimes insulted, sometimes unknown – thus lives the man of realisation, ever happy with Supreme Bliss.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Sometimes a fool, sometimes a sage, sometimes possessed of regal splendour; sometimes wandering, sometimes behaving like a motionless python, sometimes wearing a benignant expression; sometimes honoured, sometimes insulted, sometimes unknown – thus lives the man of realisation, ever happy with Supreme Bliss.

sanskrit_shloka:
निर्धनोऽपि सदा तुष्टोऽप्यसहायो महाबलः ।
नित्यतृप्तोऽप्यभुञ्जानोऽप्यसमः समदर्शनः ॥ ५४३ ॥
transliteration:
nirdhano'pi sadā tuṣṭo'pyasahāyo mahābalaḥ |
nityatṛpto'pyabhuñjāno'pyasamaḥ samadarśanaḥ || 543 ||
translation: Though without riches, yet ever content; though helpless, yet very powerful, though not enjoying the sense-objects, yet eternally satisfied; though without an exemplar, yet looking upon all with an eye of equality.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Though without riches, yet ever content; though helpless, yet very powerful, though not enjoying the sense-objects, yet eternally satisfied; though without an exemplar, yet looking upon all with an eye of equality.

sanskrit_shloka:
अपि कुर्वन्नकुर्वाणश्चाभोक्ता फलभोग्यपि ।
शरीर्यप्यशरीर्येष परिच्छिन्नोऽपि सर्वगः ॥ ५४४ ॥
transliteration:
api kurvannakurvāṇaścābhoktā phalabhogyapi |
śarīryapyaśarīryeṣa paricchinno'pi sarvagaḥ || 544 ||
translation: Though doing, yet inactive; though experiencing fruits of past actions, yet untouched by them; though possessed of a body, yet without identification with it; though limited, yet omnipresent is he.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Though doing, yet inactive; though experiencing fruits of past actions, yet untouched by them; though possessed of a body, yet without identification with it; though limited, yet omnipresent is he.

sanskrit_shloka:
अशरीरं सदा सन्तमिमं ब्रह्मविदं क्वचित् ।
प्रियाप्रिये न स्पृशतस्तथैव च शुभाशुभे ॥ ५४५ ॥
transliteration:
aśarīraṃ sadā santamimaṃ brahmavidaṃ kvacit |
priyāpriye na spṛśatastathaiva ca śubhāśubhe || 545 ||
translation: Neither pleasure nor pain, nor good nor evil, ever touches this knower of Brahman, who always lives without the body-idea.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Neither pleasure nor pain, nor good nor evil, ever touches this knower of Brahman, who always lives without the body-idea.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्थूलादिसंबन्धवतोऽभिमानिनः सुखं च दुःखं च शुभाशुभे च ।
विध्वस्तबन्धस्य सदात्मनो मुनेः कुतः शुभं वाप्यशुभं फलं वा ॥ ५४६ ॥
transliteration:
sthūlādisaṃbandhavato'bhimāninaḥ sukhaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca śubhāśubhe ca |
vidhvastabandhasya sadātmano muneḥ kutaḥ śubhaṃ vāpyaśubhaṃ phalaṃ vā || 546 ||
translation: Pleasure or pain, or good or evil, affects only him who has connections with the gross body etc., and identifies himself with these. How can good or evil, or their effects, touch the sage who has identified himself with the Reality and thereby shattered his bondage?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Pleasure or pain, or good or evil, affects only him who has connections with the gross body etc., and identifies himself with these. How can good or evil, or their effects, touch the sage who has identified himself with the Reality and thereby shattered his bondage?

sanskrit_shloka:
तमसा ग्रस्तवद्भानादग्रस्तोऽपि रविर्जनैः ।
ग्रस्त इत्युच्यते भ्रान्त्यां ह्यज्ञात्वा वस्तुलक्षणम् ॥ ५४७ ॥
transliteration:
tamasā grastavadbhānādagrasto'pi ravirjanaiḥ |
grasta ityucyate bhrāntyāṃ hyajñātvā vastulakṣaṇam || 547 ||
translation: The sun which appears to be, but is not actually, swallowed by Rāhu, is said to be swallowed, on account of delusion, by people, not knowing the real nature of the sun.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The sun which appears to be, but is not actually, swallowed by Rāhu, is said to be swallowed, on account of delusion, by people, not knowing the real nature of the sun.

sanskrit_shloka:
तद्वद्देहादिबन्धेभ्यो विमुक्तं ब्रह्मवित्तमम् ।
पश्यन्ति देहिवन्मूढाः शरीराभासदर्शनात् ॥ ५४८ ॥
transliteration:
tadvaddehādibandhebhyo vimuktaṃ brahmavittamam |
paśyanti dehivanmūḍhāḥ śarīrābhāsadarśanāt || 548 ||
translation: Similarly, ignorant people look upon the perfect knower of Brahman, who is wholly rid of bondages of the body etc., as possessed of the body, seeing but an appearance of it.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Similarly, ignorant people look upon the perfect knower of Brahman, who is wholly rid of bondages of the body etc., as possessed of the body, seeing but an appearance of it.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहिर्निर्ल्वयनीं वायं मुक्त्वा देहं तु तिष्ठति ।
इतस्ततश्चाल्यमानो यत्किंचित्प्राणवायुना ॥ ५४९ ॥
transliteration:
ahirnirlvayanīṃ vāyaṃ muktvā dehaṃ tu tiṣṭhati |
itastataścālyamāno yatkiṃcitprāṇavāyunā || 549 ||
translation: In reality, however, he rests discarding the body, like the snake its slough; and the body is moved hither and thither by the force of the Prāṇa, just as it listeth.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: In reality, however, he rests discarding the body, like the snake its slough; and the body is moved hither and thither by the force of the Prāṇa, just as it listeth.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्त्रोतसा नीयते दारु यथा निम्नोन्नतस्थलम् ।
दैवेन नीयते देहो यथाकालोपभुक्तिषु ॥ ५५0 ॥
transliteration:
strotasā nīyate dāru yathā nimnonnatasthalam |
daivena nīyate deho yathākālopabhuktiṣu || 550 ||
translation: As a piece of wood is drifted on to a high or low ground by the current, so is his body carried on by the momentum of past actions to the varied experience of their fruits, as these present themselves in due course.
